messages:
alex: Heads-up — ACME Prod (customer) reporting high 429 rate and very slow tail latencies since 13:07 UTC. Every surge hits a long scale-up (minutes).

alex: Paste of starter log: 
```
2026-03-15T13:07:21Z provisioner: request for 8 replicas -> queued
2026-03-15T13:07:25Z node-provision: pulling image x.x/acme-serving:v3.2 -> error: unauthorized: authentication required
2026-03-15T13:07:25Z kubelet: Back-off pulling image
2026-03-15T13:08:02Z autoscaler: probe backoff 60s, next probe in 45s
```

sara-oncall: omg — looks like image pull auth, not pure coldstart cpu. Any recent credential rotation?

mateo: Checking registry audit — I see a pile of 401/403s from our nodes starting 12:58 UTC. Token used by node bootstrap service account failed with "Expired token" error.

alex: ACME is on Dedicated capacity (pool-redwood-east). They said this started after we pushed a model image last night. Could be that the node bootstrap SA key expired and new nodes can't pull, so autoscaler keeps waiting.

jinx-infra: Confirmed: cluster node-pool autoscaler attempts to create VMs, but container runtime fails image pull -> nodes stay NotReady. Autoscaler sees unschedulable pods and throttles further scale due to min-backoff. Sequence: create VM -> kubelet starts -> image pull fails -> probe backoff -> no readiness -> autoscaler reduces spawn rate to avoid flapping.

alex: So this is a config/auth problem that manifests as slow autoscaling. Customer impact: 429s because minReplicas (2) insufficient for burst and warm pool is only 0.

mateo: Quick repro steps for others: 
1) Simulate by revoking the node bootstrap secret: `kubectl -n infra delete secret node-bootstrap-key`.
2) Try to spin 4 replicas: `redwoodctl scale --cluster pool-redwood-east --replicas 6`
3) Watch `kubectl get pods -w` and `journalctl -u kubelet | grep pull` -> you'll see unauthorized errors.

deploy-bot: [deploy] image-pull-failure detected on pool-redwood-east at 2026-03-15T13:07:25Z. Ticket created: SUP-12345.

sara-oncall: Immediate mitigation we can do for the customer: 1) rotate bootstrap key + re-seed node imagePullSecrets (jinx?). 2) temporarily increase warmPool to 4 or bump minReplicas to 4 so current nodes don't rely on new spinups. 3) add a short autoscaler cooldown override (30s) to let nodes finish initializations faster.

jinx-infra: On it — rotating service account now and patching imagePullSecrets cluster-wide. Running: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/key.json --iam-account=nodes@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` then recreated secret.

mateo: Also noticed the autoscaler has a long exponential backoff after repeated failed probes (we cap at 5m). For this customer the backoff is amplifying the slowdown. We should reduce max backoff for Dedicated pools to 90s as a short-term config tweak.

alex: Can we get a temporary exception so that this customer gets warmer pods while we fix auth? They're in enterprise tier.

jinx-infra: Warm pool bumped to 4 for pool-redwood-east. Rotated secret applied to new nodes (verification in progress).

sara-oncall: Monitoring — please watch error counts and scaling events. If 429s don't drop in 5 mins escalate to SRE pager.

mateo: Patch to autoscaler backoff config drafted: `autoscaler.maxProbeBackoff=90s` — will push to staging then prod for Dedicated pools if tests pass.

alex: Customer updated: we applied a temporary warm pool and rotated node bootstrap keys. Asking them to validate traffic pattern.

deploy-bot: [incident-update] SUP-12345: warm_pool=4 applied, node-bootstrap secret rotated, autoscaler_backoff_proposed=90s.

sara-oncall: Follow-ups: 1) investigate why bootstrap key expired without alert (pager rule missing). 2) add health-check gating earlier to detect image-pull auth failures and surface them in console. 3) longer term: support cached internal images or mirrored registry for Dedicated pools to avoid external rate limits.

alex: Thanks team. I’ll keep thread open until customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
